Find the arc length $L$ of the polar curve $r=3\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta $ for $\frac{\pi }{2}\le \theta \le \frac{5\pi }{6}$ (shown in blue in the diagram above). Do not round the answer.

$L=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
The arc length $L$ of a polar curve $r=r(\theta )$ is given by

$$
L={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

Since $r=3\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,$ we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta }=3\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta .
$$

Therefore, the arc length is

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{5\pi /6}\sqrt{{(3\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )}^{2}+{(3\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{5\pi /6}\sqrt{9{sin}^{2}⁡\theta +9{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{5\pi /6}\sqrt{9}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{5\pi /6}3\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =3\theta \,{|}_{\pi /2}^{5\pi /6} \\  & =3(\frac{5\pi }{6}-\frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & =\pi .\end{aligned}
$$
